commits.subject: Merge pull request #600 from SDiestelmann/feat/delphi-aarch64-stubs
commits.body: core: external interface aarch64 stubs for the Delphi Android and iOS compilers
commits.author: ab

files.patch:
@@ -2,4 +2,10 @@
 
 gcc -c delphi-linux-x64.s -o delphi-linux-x64.o
 
-
+# aarch64 needs the preprocessor, and one object per binary format/platform:
+# use the clang of the NDK shipped with the RAD Studio Android SDK
+CLANG=${CLANG:-clang}
+ASM="-x assembler-with-cpp -c delphi-aarch64.s"
+$CLANG $ASM --target=aarch64-linux-android23 -o delphi-android-arm64.o
+$CLANG $ASM --target=arm64-apple-ios15.0 -o delphi-ios-arm64.o
+$CLANG $ASM --target=arm64-apple-ios15.0-simulator -o delphi-iossim-arm64.o

@@ -0,0 +1,197 @@
+// interface stubs for the Delphi LLVM aarch64 compilers (Android and iOS):
+//   aarch64fakestub   = TInterfacedObjectFake methods (SOA client side)
+//   aarch64callmethod = CallMethod() for RawExecute (SOA server side, callbacks)
+//   aarch64fakethunks = the VMT entry points, one per method index
+// counterpart of delphi-linux-x64.s, used by mormot.core.interfaces.pas
+// when DELPHI_AARCH64_RESULT_X8 is defined
+//
+// build with the clang of the NDK shipped with the RAD Studio Android SDK
+// (see compile.sh - the same source yields ELF for Android, Mach-O for iOS)
+//
+// aarch64fakestub is entered from one of the thunks below, with
+//   X16 = method index, X0 = interface instance,
+//   X1..X7 / D0..D7 / stack = parameters, X8 = by-ref result (AAPCS64)
+// it builds a TFakeCallStack (ABIA64 layout) on the stack:
+//   +0   ParamRegs   X0..X7
+//   +64  FPRegs      D0..D7
+//   +128 MethodIndex (X16)
+//   +136 Frame       = X8, the indirect result pointer used by Delphi
+//   +144 Ret         = saved X29
+//   +152 DummyStack  = saved X30
+//   +160 Stack       = caller stack arguments
+// then calls fakecall(Instance = X0, Stack = SP), i.e. the exported
+// TInterfacedObjectFakeRaw.FakeCall redirection, which returns the ordinal
+// result in X0 and stores any float result into FPRegs[D0]
+//
+// NOTE: the .cfi_* directives are mandatory: Delphi uses DWARF exceptions, so
+// an exception raised within FakeCall must be able to unwind through this frame
+
+
+#if defined(__MACH__)
+  // Mach-O prefixes every symbol with an underscore - as does the Delphi iOS
+  // compiler - knows no ELF symbol attributes, and starts local labels with L
+  #define SYM(name) _##name
+  #define FUNC_TYPE(name)
+  #define FUNC_SIZE(name)
+  #define LOCAL(name) L##name
+#else
+  #define SYM(name) name
+  #define FUNC_TYPE(name) .type name, %function
+  #define FUNC_SIZE(name) .size name, .-name
+  #define LOCAL(name) .L##name
+#endif
+
+    .text
+    .p2align 2
+    .global SYM(aarch64fakestub)
+    FUNC_TYPE(SYM(aarch64fakestub))
+
+SYM(aarch64fakestub):
+    .cfi_startproc
+    stp x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!
+    .cfi_def_cfa_offset 16
+    .cfi_offset x29, -16
+    .cfi_offset x30, -8
+    mov x29, sp
+    .cfi_def_cfa x29, 16
+    sub sp, sp, #144
+
+    stp x0, x1, [sp, #0]
+    stp x2, x3, [sp, #16]
+    stp x4, x5, [sp, #32]
+    stp x6, x7, [sp, #48]
+    stp d0, d1, [sp, #64]
+    stp d2, d3, [sp, #80]
+    stp d4, d5, [sp, #96]
+    stp d6, d7, [sp, #112]
+    stp x16, x8, [sp, #128]
+
+    mov x1, sp
+    bl  SYM(fakecall)
+
+    // FakeCall stored any float result into FPRegs[D0]
+    ldr d0, [sp, #64]
+
+    mov sp, x29
+    ldp x29, x30, [sp], #16
+    .cfi_def_cfa sp, 0
+    .cfi_restore x29
+    .cfi_restore x30
+    ret
+    .cfi_endproc
+    FUNC_SIZE(SYM(aarch64fakestub))
+
+
+// the VMT entry points, one per method index - the Pascal side used to JIT these
+// two instructions per index into an anonymous rwx page, which iOS kills on sight
+// ("KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE ... CODESIGNING, Invalid Page"): a normal app may not
+// run code it wrote itself. Compiled in, they cost 8 bytes each.
+// - the count has to match MAX_METHOD_COUNT of mormot.core.interfaces (a
+//   {$message fatal} there guards the other direction)
+// - entry i is aarch64fakethunks + i * 8, and does what the JITted stub did:
+//   method index into X16, then on to aarch64fakestub (b reaches +-128 MB, and
+//   both live in the same section)
+
+    .p2align 2
+    .global SYM(aarch64fakethunks)
+    FUNC_TYPE(SYM(aarch64fakethunks))
+
+SYM(aarch64fakethunks):
+    .set fakethunkindex, 0
+    .rept 128
+    movz x16, #fakethunkindex
+    b    SYM(aarch64fakestub)
+    .set fakethunkindex, fakethunkindex + 1
+    .endr
+    FUNC_SIZE(SYM(aarch64fakethunks))
+
+// the address of that table, as a function - Delphi wraps an "external ...

commits.subject: tools: LogView remote logging with any client layout - fix #344
commits.body:
TSynLogFile detects the layout of its rows once, whereas remote clients may
use calendar, zoned or high resolution timestamps, with or without a
ptIdentifiedInOneFile thread column. In remote mode, the viewer banner fixed
a layout without thread column, so every later row of a thread-identified
client failed the level detection and was never displayed.

New mormot.tools.logview.remote unit with TRemoteLogNormalizer, which
rewrites every received row into one layout - calendar timestamp, thread
column and level - before TSynLogFileView.AddInMemoryLine():
- thread numbers are made unique per client connection, as given by the new
  TRestHttpRemoteLogServer.CreateWithSender, and named after their sender
- high resolution timestamps are relative to the log start of the client,
  which is not transmitted: the UTC receipt time is used, and the original
  counter is kept as "[hires ...]" in the text
- a row which is not a TSynLog row is kept as text of its connection

The rows are still queued by the HTTP server thread, and now normalized by
the UI thread, which also maintains the live thread list, the thread filter,
and follows the last row only when it is already visible.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

+unit mormot.tools.logview.remote;
+
+{
+  *****************************************************************************
+
+   Normalize Remote TSynLog Rows for the mORMot LogView Tool
+    - Rewrite any Received Row into the Single Layout of a TSynLogFileView
+    - Unique Thread Numbers per Client Connection
+
+  *****************************************************************************
+}
+
+interface
+
+{$I ..\..\mormot.defines.inc}
+
+uses
+  sysutils,
+  mormot.core.base,
+  mormot.core.os,
+  mormot.core.unicode,
+  mormot.core.text,
+  mormot.core.datetime,
+  mormot.core.log;
+
+const
+  /// the thread number of the rows generated by the viewer itself
+  // - TSynLogFile.ThreadName() always names thread 1 "Main Thread"
+  REMOTE_VIEWER_THREAD = 1;
+  /// the thread numbers are stored as word in TSynLogFile.EventThread[]
+  REMOTE_MAX_THREAD = 65535;
+
+type
+  /// how a received row was recognized by TRemoteLogNormalizer.Normalize
+  TRemoteRowKind = (
+    rrkCalendar,
+    rrkZoned,
+    rrkHighRes,
+    rrkText);
+

+  // - TSynLogFile detects the layout of its rows once, whereas remote clients
+  // may use calendar, zoned or high resolution timestamps, with or without a
+  // ptIdentifiedInOneFile thread column - see issue #344
+  // - output is always a 17 chars calendar timestamp, a 3 chars thread column
+  // and the 7 chars level text, as the Banner() row which should come first
+  // - thread numbers are unique per client connection: REMOTE_VIEWER_THREAD for
+  // the viewer rows, then 2..REMOTE_MAX_THREAD for each (connection, thread)
+  // - high resolution timestamps are relative to the log start of the client,
+  // which is not transmitted: the receipt time is used instead, and the text is
+  // prefixed with the original counter - but for sllEnter, to keep the
+  // profiling by method name
+  // - an unrecognized row is kept as sllInfo text of its connection
+  // - this class is not thread-safe: use it from a single thread only
+  TRemoteLogNormalizer = class
+  protected
+    fKeys: TRawUtf8DynArray; // 'connection:thread' of thread 2,3,4...
+    fKeysCount: integer;
+    fLastConnection: Int64; // most rows come from the same thread in a row
+    fLastOrig, fLastThread: cardinal;
+    fNames: TRawUtf8DynArray; // [thread - 2] = latest name of this thread

commits.subject: rest: TRestHttpRemoteLogServer.CreateWithSender
commits.body:
A new TRemoteLogReceivedFrom callback also receives the connection ID and the
remote IP of the request, so that a viewer can tell several simultaneous
remote log clients apart - as needed by the LogView port (#588) to keep the
thread numbers of each client separated. The existing Create() and its
TRemoteLogReceivedOne callback are unchanged.

The connection ID identifies the HTTP connection, not the client process: a
reconnecting client gets a new ID, and an ID may be reused after a while.

Also assign the callback before the inherited constructor starts the HTTP
server: a request received meanwhile did find no callback, and was silently
answered without Ctxt.Success.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

commits.subject: tools: port the mORMot 1 LogView sample as a FPC/Lazarus LCL app
commits.body:
First step of #588: the form and the .log file viewing, on top of the
existing TSynLogFileView of mormot.core.log.

Beside the plain port (TSynLogInfo -> TSynLogLevel, AlgoSynLZ, TDebugFile,
TRestHttpRemoteLogServer), this fixes some issues of the original sample:
- remote rows were appended from the HTTP server thread while the UI thread
  was drawing: they are now queued, then applied by the refresh timer
- fixed pixel sizes clipped text and overflowed the left panel with current
  fonts and DPI: row heights, column widths and layout use font metrics
- the Stats dialog now also shows ARM 32-bit/64-bit CPU features
- grid index out of range when a thread filter selects no row
- plain text copy, elapsed time on filtered rows, search highlight offsets
- the address lookup accepts .mab only, and does not use TDebugFile.Create
  cache maintenance, which could delete an unreadable .mab file
- opening a file stops the remote server, and every view transition
  resets the thread panel, profiler and event list state
commits.author: Sven Harazim
